claim:
Let \(X=\ell_2-\ell_1\) be the real Day--James plane with
\[
\|(s,t)\|_X=
\begin{cases}
\sqrt{s^2+t^2},&st\ge0,\\
|s|+|t|,&st\le0.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(\varepsilon\in[0,1)\), write \(u\perp_D^\varepsilon v\) when
\[
\|u+\lambda v\|_X\ge\sqrt{1-\varepsilon^2}\,\|u\|_X
\qquad(\lambda\in\mathbb R).
\]
Then the least \(\varepsilon\) for which
\[
x\perp_B y\Longrightarrow y\perp_D^\varepsilon x
\qquad(x,y\in X)
\]
is
\[
\varepsilon_D(X)=\frac1{\sqrt2}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\inf_{\substack{x,y\in S_X\\x\perp_B y}}
\inf_{\lambda\in\mathbb R}\|y+\lambda x\|_X
=
\frac1{\sqrt2}.
\]
Equality is attained by
\[
x=(1,0),
\qquad
y=\frac{(1,1)}{\sqrt2},
\]
and by the norm symmetries.

correctness.rationale: The unit sphere is exhaustively split into Euclidean arcs, taxicab facets, and coordinate-axis junctions. Smooth points have forced Birkhoff directions from unique norming functionals, while axes use the complete norming-functional segment. In every stratum the reverse distance is computed exactly by the quotient-space formula for an annihilating functional. Every value is at least 1/sqrt(2), and the axis/diagonal pair attains equality.
risks: The proof is specific to p=2.
The modified Dragomir sqrt(1-epsilon^2) normalization is essential.

value.rationale: Modified-Dragomir symmetry quantifies the failure of Birkhoff--James orthogonality to be symmetric. General theory proves existence in every finite-dimensional Banach space but leaves optimal constants open. The Day--James ell_2-ell_1 plane is a classical exact benchmark, and the sharp value identifies a structural boundary phenomenon: the worst reverse asymmetry occurs at a nonsmooth axis junction while both smooth strata have no smaller reverse distance.
risks: The result is one exact benchmark rather than a complete p-dependent theory.
